title: Freeze provider-run decision identity
description: Prerequisite for the strict reader in task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8. The provider-run writer's command kind is currently a private literal in provider-run-ledger.ts, so a reader must either duplicate it or omit a binding check. Promote that exact existing kind to the provider-run contract and keep the production writer and its receipt tests pinned to the single source.
definitionOfDone: The existing `provider-run.telemetry.commit` value is exported once as a frozen literal from provider-run-contracts.ts and provider-run-ledger.ts imports it; no second production or test literal owns the command identity.

The production ledger's real SqliteEventStore decision trace and command decision both carry the exported kind, with target aggregate, expected version, request digest, singleton event id, and result bytes unchanged.

Focused ledger tests assert the exact command kind on the stored event, decision and receipt-backed trace, plus a positive accepted commit and replay control; mutating the writer to a different kind reddens the named binding assertion.
Daemon typecheck/test execute with nonzero count lines, and completion names the provider-run reader child of task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8 as consumer.
taskRails: Own only apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts, provider-run-ledger.ts, and provider-run-ledger.test.ts; do not change the record/event schema or command bytes.
This is a constant-promotion and production-binding slice, not a new wire kind; do not register it in RuntimeCommandKind or HTTP.
Preserve all existing ledger/store refusal mappings and exact layers; use TDD and explicit owned-path commit.

implementationPlan.description: Verify, then RED. The private literal is confirmed at apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.ts:56 `const COMMAND_KIND = "provider-run.telemetry.commit"`, used at :215; provider-run-contracts.ts already owns the sibling frozen identities (PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION :57, PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE :60), so the new export sits beside them in the same `as const` style. SIZE CAUTION: the ledger file is 248 lines -- two from the 250 target -- so the edit must be net-neutral or negative (the removed const line pays for the import line; do not add anything else there). RED first, in the existing provider-run-ledger.test.ts: extend the accepted-commit and replay controls to assert the exact command kind ON THE STORED ARTIFACTS -- the durable event's decision trace, the command decision record, and the receipt-backed trace -- imported from provider-run-contracts.ts, NOT retyped in the test; a test literal would be the second owner the DoD forbids. The assertions must read the kind from durable bytes, because an assertion against the writer's input echoes whatever the writer sent.
implementationPlan.note:
VERIFIED, THEN RED. Measured at HEAD c03bb1b.

PREMISES CONFIRMED, all four, and the strongest one is the grep. `git grep -n "provider-run.telemetry.commit"` across apps/daemon, packages, adapters and tests returns EXACTLY ONE line repo-wide:
    apps/daemon/src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.ts:56:const COMMAND_KIND = "provider-run.telemetry.commit";
So there is no second production owner and no test literal today — promotion cannot silently fork an identity, and the "no second owner" clause of DoD 1 starts from a clean base. Sole use is :215 inside `store.commitExpectedVersionDecision({ commandKind: COMMAND_KIND, ... })`. Sibling identities confirmed in contracts: `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION` :57 and `PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE` :60, both `... as const`, so the new export has an established style to match. Line counts: contracts 204, ledger 248 (two under the 250 target, so the step-2 edit must be net-neutral), test 552. Owned paths clean, no peer contention.

WHICH DURABLE ARTIFACTS ACTUALLY CARRY THE KIND — measured in the store contracts rather than assumed, and one of the three named in the plan does NOT:
 - `StoredEvent.decisionTrace.commandKind` (store-contracts.ts:156-163) — the durable event's decision trace. Present.
 - `CommandDecisionRecordBase.commandKind` (:88), returned by `store.getCommandDecision(key)`. Present.
 - `CommandReceipt` (:138-149) has NO `commandKind` field at all — it carries aggregateId, commandId, committedAt, currentVersion, effectIdentityVersion, effectSha256, eventIds, outboxMessageIds, previousVersion, requestSha256. So "the receipt-backed trace" cannot mean a kind read off the receipt; there is none to read. I implemented it the only way that is both honest and receipt-backed: use `getCommandReceipt(commandId).eventIds` to NAME the committed event, then read THAT event's `decisionTrace.commandKind`. The receipt selects the artifact; the artifact carries the kind.

THE ECHO TRAP, closed deliberately. planningNotes names it as risk 1 and it is the whole reason this test can be worth anything: an assertion against `input()` or against the returned `ProviderRunCommitResult` reads back the writer's own argument and stays green no matter what was actually stored. Every assertion I added reads from the STORE — `store.readEvents(...)`, `store.getCommandDecision(...)`, `store.getCommandReceipt(...)` — and the comment in the test says so, so a later editor cannot quietly "simplify" it into an echo.

NO TEST LITERAL, WHICH REQUIRED RESISTING AN OBVIOUS ASSERTION. My first draft ended with `expect(PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND).toBe("provider-run.telemetry.commit")` to pin the wire value. I removed it: DoD 1 forbids a second literal owning the identity in production OR TEST, and that line would have been exactly that. The consequence is worth stating plainly for QA — because both operands of the remaining assertions now come from the same constant, those assertions cannot detect a change to the VALUE, only a break in the BINDING. That is the correct division: single ownership is the DoD's requirement, and the step-3 drill is what makes the operands diverge and proves the binding is real. `grep -c "provider-run.telemetry.commit"` in the test file is 0.

RED, ON BOTH LEGS, FOR EXACTLY ONE REASON:
 - typecheck: EXIT=1, a single diagnostic — `src/telemetry/provider-run-ledger.test.ts(31,3): error TS2305: Module '"./provider-run-contracts.js"' has no exported member 'PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND'.`
 - test: EXIT=1, `Test Files 1 failed | 130 passed (131)`, `Tests 2 failed | 2828 passed (2830)`. The two failures are precisely the two tests I added, at :218 and :322. Nothing else in the daemon suite moved.
Daemon baseline for the final gate to reproduce: 131 test files, 2830 tests.

Production is still untouched; the constant lands in step 2.

Grep afterward that exactly ONE production definition of the string exists: `git grep -n "provider-run.telemetry.commit" apps/daemon/src/ | grep -v '\.test\.'` must show the contracts export and the ledger import site only. Do NOT register the kind in RuntimeCommandKind or HTTP (rail: this is constant promotion, not a wire kind -- the frozen runtime vocabulary has a full-coverage ratchet and touching it is a different, larger task).
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. typecheck EXIT=0 with zero diagnostics; test EXIT=0, `Test Files 131 passed (131)` / `Tests 2830 passed (2830)` — the same total as the step-1 RED baseline, with the 2 failures now passing.

THE PROMOTION, three lines of real change:
 - contracts: `export const PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND = "provider-run.telemetry.commit" as const;` placed beside `PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION` and `PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE`, matching their `as const` style, with a comment explaining why single ownership matters (the store's replay identity hashes this kind with the key and target aggregate, so a reader holding its own copy could drift while both suites stayed green).
 - ledger: private `const COMMAND_KIND` at :56 DELETED, `PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND` added to the EXISTING contracts import block at :45, call site now reads `commandKind: PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND`.

LINE BUDGET HELD EXACTLY AS PLANNED: the ledger is still **248** lines — the deleted const paid for the import line, net zero, two under the 250 target. Contracts 204 -> 213, far under. Nothing else was added to the ledger.

DoD 1 SATISFIED BY MEASUREMENT: `git grep -n "provider-run.telemetry.commit"` across apps/daemon, packages, adapters and tests now returns EXACTLY ONE line, `provider-run-contracts.ts:69`. One owner, production or test. The test file contains zero occurrences of the string (it imports the constant), so no second owner was introduced by the tests either.

IDENTITY FIELDS UNCHANGED, per DoD 2 and rail 1: aggregate derivation, expected version, request digest, singleton event id and result bytes were not touched — the diff in the ledger is one import line, one deleted const line, and one identifier at the call site. The VALUE reaching `commandKind:` is byte-identical; only the name that carries it changed, since the local const no longer exists. Not registered in RuntimeCommandKind or HTTP (rail 2).

A REAL FINDING THAT CHANGED THE TEST, and it matters for the sibling reader task. The plan asked for the kind to be asserted on "the receipt-backed trace". I wrote that arm against `store.getCommandReceipt(KEY.commandId)` and it FAILED with `AssertionError: Target cannot be null or undefined` — the receipt came back null. That is not a bug in my test setup; it is how the store works, and I traced it rather than working around it:
 - `CommandReceipt` (store-contracts.ts:138-149) carries NO `commandKind` field at all.
 - Receipts are stored under `identities.receiptCommandId`, and `receiptCommandId = internalReceiptCommandId(decisionId)` = `` `${INTERNAL_IDENTIFIER_PREFIX}decision-effect:${decisionId}` `` (store-digests.ts:104-106) — an INTERNAL derived id, never the caller's `commandId`.
 - Neither `internalReceiptCommandId` nor `identifyCommandDecisionId` is exported from the store package root (`git grep` over packages/store/src/index.ts is empty).
So a consumer holding only a `CommandDecisionKey` CANNOT address the receipt, and a test that rebuilt that string would be reimplementing store authority inside the test — which the global rail forbids and which would silently rot if the prefix ever changed.
I rewired the third arm onto the public equivalent: `getCommandDecision(KEY).businessEventIds` names the event the decision sealed, and that named event's `decisionTrace.commandKind` is read back. Deliberately routed through the effect record rather than `events[0]`, so it is a third INDEPENDENT binding rather than a restatement of the first assertion. The reason is written into the test comment so nobody "restores" the receipt call later.
FLAGGING FOR THE CONSUMER: task-00e4827d's reader child has a DoD clause reading "`getCommandDecision` and `getCommandReceipt` must prove EFFECTS_COMMITTED 0->1, exact target, singleton event, result bytes/effect digest and zero outbox". Its `getCommandReceipt` half is not reachable the way that phrasing implies — `outboxMessageIds` and the 0->1 version pair live on the receipt, which cannot be fetched with the caller's command id. That task will need either a store change or those proofs taken from the decision record (`businessEventIds`, `expectedVersion`/`observedVersion`, `outboxMessageIds`, `effectSha256`, `resultBytes` are all on `CommandDecisionRecordBase`). Better found now than at that task's gate.

Drill, commit and gate are step 3.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Trivial constant-promotion slice; per the planning skill's skip table it gets a compact plan (verify+RED, GREEN, drill+gate) rather than the 8-phase skeleton. The only decisions: (a) export name PROVIDER_RUN_COMMAND_KIND matching the sibling PROVIDER_RUN_* naming in contracts; (b) net-neutral edit discipline in the ledger because it sits at 248/250 lines; (c) the test imports the constant rather than retyping it -- a retyped test literal would be a second owner of the identity, exactly what the DoD's 'no second production or test literal' clause forbids, and it would keep passing if the production value drifted. REJECTED: registering the kind in RuntimeCommandKind (rail forbids; frozen vocabulary with full-coverage ratchet); moving the aggregate-derivation namespace or any other identity while in the file (scope creep in a two-line task).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured at current HEAD: private literal at provider-run-ledger.ts:56, sole use :215; ledger header comment (:149-151) documents that the store's replay identity hashes key, commandKind and targetAggregateId with constant commandKind/expectedVersion -- which is WHY the reader task (00e4827d's child) needs the exported kind for its binding check rather than duplicating the string. provider-run-contracts.ts (204 lines) owns PROVIDER_RUN_RECORD_VERSION (:57), PROVIDER_RUN_EVENT_TYPE (:60) and AGGREGATE_NAMESPACE (:163); the new export joins that family. Ledger file is 248 lines -- delete-const-add-import keeps it neutral. Only one production occurrence of the string exists today (grep verified), so promotion cannot silently fork an identity.
planningNotes.risks: Small but two real traps: (1) the echo assertion -- a test asserting the kind on the writer's INPUT or on the returned result object passes regardless of what was stored; the binding assertions must decode the durable event/decision/receipt, and the drill's red must land on exactly that assertion; (2) the 248-line ledger file -- any extra addition there crosses the target; keep the edit to remove-one-line-add-one-line. Also preserve every existing refusal mapping untouched; this task changes identity OWNERSHIP, not behavior, and QA should see a diff of ~4 lines production plus test assertions.
